title: Book Three · Chapter 9: A Fish on the Board
story:
Rain hits the classroom windows on Monday.

Ronan finishes his lunch and looks outside. Water runs down the steps. The field is empty.

The boy at the next desk looks at his ball.

“No,” Ronan says.

“I didn't say anything.”

“Your hands did.”

The boy puts the ball under his chair.

At the front, a girl picks up some chalk. She draws three short lines on the board. Then she adds a round shape.

“Guess,” she says.

“A table.”

“A dog.”

“Your lunch.”

The girl adds two long ears.

“A rabbit!” someone calls.

She turns around and smiles. Another girl gets up to draw. Several students move closer.

Ronan stays at his desk. He can see the board from there.

The next drawing is a shoe. The next is a tree. One boy draws a face with a very large nose.

“You,” his friend says.

“No. My uncle.”

The room fills with laughter. Outside, the rain grows louder.

“Your turn,” the boy at the next desk tells Ronan.

“I can't draw well.”

“Look at that nose. You can draw here.”

Ronan stands up. At the board, he takes a short piece of chalk. He wants to draw a fish. He draws a long body and a tail.

“A leaf,” someone says.

Ronan adds an eye.

“A leaf with an eye.”

He draws a fin on the back. Then he adds a mouth. The mouth takes up too much space.

“A fish?” the first girl asks.

“Yes.”

“A hungry fish,” the boy from his desk says.

Anna comes in with her friend. They shake rain from a small umbrella near the door.

Anna looks at the board.

“Is it eating the tree?”

The old tree drawing is still beside the fish. Ronan looks at the open mouth and the nearest branch.

He draws a little apple on the branch.

“Only the fruit.”

Anna laughs. Her friend guesses an apple fish. Someone asks for legs.

Ronan puts the chalk down.

“It is your fish now.”

The boy from his desk gets up. Soon the fish has four short legs and a hat.

Ronan returns to his seat. There is chalk on his fingers. Anna offers him a piece of paper, and he wipes his hands.

The bell rings. The boy at the front puts down the chalk and cleans the board. The fish disappears first. Then the tree and the large nose are gone.

The teacher comes in and puts a wet umbrella beside the door.

Everyone settles down. Ronan opens his exercise book.

At the bottom of his page, he draws one small fish. He gives this one a smaller mouth.

Anna sees it and whispers, “No lunch today?”

He draws an apple beside it before he turns the page.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

chalk＝粉笔；guess＝猜；fin＝鱼鳍；wipe＝擦。

## 理解问题

1. 为什么大家这天午间留在教室玩猜画？
2. Ronan最初画的鱼为什么让人猜成叶子？同学后来给它添了什么？

## 读句子

**She draws three short lines on the board.**

拆开看：She / draws three short lines / on the board.

她／画了三条短线／画在黑板上。
